sentences.zh: 这些选民帮助总统在上一次选举中获得了普选票的多数。

sentences.en: They're what made his coalition seem so formidable and raised all the talk of a realignment, and he did not reward them for that.
sentences.zh: 他们让他的联盟看起来如此强大，并引发了所有关于重组的讨论，但他并没有因此奖励他们。

sentences.en: And if anything, he pursued policies that assured that he would lose all of the gains that he made and more.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是他推行的政策确保了他会失去他所取得的所有成果，甚至更多。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: It's also worth talking about the voters who didn't show up in the states where we have data.
sentences.zh: 同样值得讨论的是那些在有数据的州没有出来投票的选民。

sentences.en: There's a lot of evidence that white Republicans were less likely to vote in this election than they have been in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明，白人共和党人在这次选举中投票的可能性比过去要小。

sentences.en: It's even true in states like Florida, where the Republicans fared relatively well.
sentences.zh: 即使在佛罗里达州这样的州也是如此，共和党人在那里表现相对较好。

sentences.en: And in particular, there's evidence that young white Republicans really didn't show up at all.
sentences.zh: 特别是，有证据表明年轻的白人共和党人确实根本没有出来投票。

sentences.en: And stepping back to where we were two years ago, remember how the Republicans seem to make extraordinary gains among young men who,
sentences.zh: 回顾两年前，还记得共和党人似乎在年轻男性中取得了非凡的收益吗，

sentences.en: by our estimates, voted for Trump by a wide margin in the last election, more than 10 points.
sentences.zh: 根据我们的估计，他们在上次选举中以很大优势投票给特朗普，超过10个百分点。

sentences.en: We have the Democrats getting more than 60 percent of young men in this election.
sentences.zh: 这次选举中，民主党获得了超过60%的年轻男性选票。

sentences.en: And, yeah, that's partly because there are people who flipped their votes, who thought, you know, they wanted Trump for low prices and this isn't what they got.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，这部分是因为有些人改变了投票意向，他们认为，你知道，他们想要特朗普带来低物价，但这并不是他们得到的。

sentences.en: But it's also because a lot of young Republicans just did not turn out and vote in this election.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为许多年轻的共和党人根本没有出来参加这次选举投票。

sentences.en: Perhaps because what they imagined as the promise of him improving their economic lot just didn't come to fruition.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为他们想象中他改善他们经济状况的承诺并没有实现。

sentences.en: So they say don't.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说不。

sentences.en: Or the war in Iran.
sentences.zh: 或者伊朗战争。

sentences.en: I mean, fundamentally, this is another group of voters that didn't get what they thought they were going to get from the president.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从根本上说，这是另一群没有从总统那里得到他们认为会得到的东西的选民。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So a more diverse electorate that favored Democrats is a real learning from the results of this midterm.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个更倾向于民主党的多元化选民群体是这次中期选举结果的一个真正教训。

sentences.en: Let's turn now to the candidates because, Nate, on Tuesday night, your second of three appearances on the show.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们转向候选人的话题，因为内特，周二晚上是你第三次上节目中的第二次。

sentences.en: How could I forget?
sentences.zh: 我怎么会忘呢？

sentences.en: You started to posit the theory that progressive candidates on the Democratic side were performing worse than some of their moderate counterparts.
sentences.zh: 你当时提出了一个理论，即民主党阵营中的进步派候选人表现不如他们的一些温和派同行。

sentences.en: And sometimes these progressives were still winning, but by meaningfully less than the moderates.
sentences.zh: 而且有时这些进步派候选人虽然赢了，但胜出的幅度明显小于温和派。

sentences.en: In the light of day, with more results now in, more time to study them, how sturdy is that theory feeling to you?
sentences.zh: 如今真相大白，有了更多的结果，也有了更多时间去研究，你觉得那个理论现在看起来有多稳固？

sentences.en: That theory seems even more sturdy.
sentences.zh: 那个理论看起来甚至更加稳固了。

sentences.en: It's worth noting, by the way, that there's a big chunk of the country that's still counting votes in California.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，值得注意的是，加利福尼亚州还有很大一部分选票仍在统计中。

sentences.en: Maybe the progressives will have some exciting victories there that show real strength.
sentences.zh: 也许进步派在那里会取得一些令人兴奋的胜利，展现出真正的实力。

sentences.en: But in the places where the vote is done, it is very hard to find a race with a high-profile progressive who is not underperforming in this election.
sentences.zh: 但在计票已经结束的地方，很难找到一位表现不佳的高知名度进步派候选人。

sentences.en: Just give us some examples.
sentences.zh: 给我们举几个例子吧。

sentences.en: And as you're doing that, let's define that word.
sentences.zh: 在你举例的同时，让我们先定义一下这个词。

sentences.en: Yeah, underperformance is a real – oh, well, those – Or both of these words are worth talking about.
sentences.zh: 没错，表现不佳是一个真正的——哦，好吧，这两个词都值得讨论。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 请继续。

sentences.en: Progressive is a hard word to define.
sentences.zh: “进步派”这个词很难定义。

sentences.en: It's a category that people could use to define anyone from a Democratic socialist to a mainstream Democrat like Barack Obama could be called a progressive.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可以用来定义任何人的类别，从民主社会主义者到像巴拉克·奥巴马这样的主流民主党人，都可以被称为进步派。

sentences.en: But what I'm really talking about here is a narrower group of progressive candidates backed by progressive activists who campaigned against the Democratic Party's establishment,
sentences.zh: 但我这里真正指的是一群更狭义的进步派候选人，他们得到进步派活动人士的支持，竞选时反对民主党的建制派，

sentences.en: who wanted the party to move towards the left, who don't merely support Medicare for All or oppose Israel, which a majority of congressional Democrats do,
sentences.zh: 他们希望党向左转，他们不仅仅是支持全民医保或反对以色列——大多数国会民主党人都这样做，

sentences.en: but are the kind of people who stake their campaigns on the issues that progressive activists care about moSt.
sentences.zh: 而是那种将竞选赌注押在进步派活动人士最关心的议题上的人。

sentences.en: They're the kind of candidates who prevailed in closely contested primaries this year.
sentences.zh: 他们就是今年在竞争激烈的初选中获胜的那类候选人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like Abdul El-Sayed as one example in a high-profile Senate race.
sentences.zh: 比如阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德，他就是高知名度参议院竞选中的一个例子。

sentences.en: Or Angie Nixon in Florida.
sentences.zh: 或者佛罗里达州的安吉·尼克松。

sentences.en: Or Angie Nixon in Florida.
sentences.zh: 或者佛罗里达州的安吉·尼克松。

sentences.en: And across the board, these candidates are doing worse than you would expect in this national and political environment.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这些候选人在当前全国政治环境下的表现比你预期的要差。

sentences.en: And I think it's worth dwelling on this point, too, here, because it's complicated in an election where the Democrats have won big.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点也值得深究，因为在民主党大获全胜的选举中，情况很复杂。

sentences.en: But because the Democrats have won so big in this election, many of the progressive candidates in question here, including Dr. El-Sayed, won.
sentences.zh: 但正因为民主党在这次选举中大获全胜，这里提到的许多进步派候选人，包括埃尔-赛义德博士，都赢了。

sentences.en: But they did not do as well as you would expect given the national political environment or as well as the other Democrats on the ballot in their same state.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到全国政治环境，或者与同州选票上的其他民主党人相比，他们的表现并没有达到预期。

sentences.en: Yeah, just specify that math.
sentences.zh: 没错，具体说说那个数据吧。

sentences.en: So let's look.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看。

sentences.en: Michigan's a good one.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州是个很好的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a state that is an easy one because Michigan voted for Trump by one and a half points, just like the country did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那个州很容易分析，因为密歇根州以1.5个百分点的优势投票给了特朗普，就像全国的情况一样。

sentences.en: The country voted for Democrats by 13.
sentences.zh: 全国以13个百分点的优势投票给了民主党。

sentences.en: We would thus expect Democrats to win in Michigan by 13.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们预计民主党在密歇根州会以13个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: El-Sayed won by seven.
sentences.zh: 埃尔-赛义德以7个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: It's also worth noting that Democratic candidates for House, in our view, are on track to win by about 11.
sentences.zh: 同样值得注意的是，在我们看来，民主党众议院候选人有望以约11个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: So that's a six or so point underperformance for El-Sayed in Michigan compared to what you would expect given what we know about what happened nationwide.
sentences.zh: 所以，考虑到我们对全国情况的了解，埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州的表现比预期低了大约6个百分点。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And when you roll that story across all the high-profile progress in this election, Angie Nixon in Florida, staying in Michigan, Will Lawrence in Michigan 7th District,
sentences.zh: 当你把这个情况应用到这次选举中所有高知名度的进步派候选人身上时，比如佛罗里达州的安吉·尼克松，留在密歇根州，密歇根州第七选区的威尔·劳伦斯，

sentences.en: Matt Dunlap in Maine 2nd.
sentences.zh: 缅因州第二选区的马特·邓拉普。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just every case at this point in a high-profile contested race where there was a big primary,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在目前所有经过大型初选的高知名度竞争激烈的选区中，每一个案例都是如此，

sentences.en: the progressive candidate in the general election has gone on to underperform.
sentences.zh: 进步派候选人在大选中的表现都低于预期。

sentences.en: And it's just hard to find counter examples.
sentences.zh: 而且很难找到反例。

sentences.en: I want to latch on to Angie Nixon in Florida, who got really close, I think within about two points.
sentences.zh: 我想抓住佛罗里达州的安吉·尼克松这个例子，她离胜利非常近，我想大约在两个百分点以内。

sentences.en: Yeah, three points, I think, in the end.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想最后是三个百分点。

sentences.en: The point of winning that Senate race as a Democratic Socialist of America candidate, to the untrained eye, by which I mean me, it would appear that her candidacy,
sentences.zh: 作为美国民主社会主义者候选人赢得那场参议院竞选的意义，在外行——也就是我——看来，似乎她的竞选，

sentences.en: how close she got to winning, seems like a shining example of how well a progressive candidate did on Tuesday night.
sentences.zh: 她离胜利有多近，看起来像是进步派候选人在周二晚上表现出色的一个光辉榜样。

sentences.en: You're saying, no, you simpleton.
sentences.zh: 你是说，不，你这个笨蛋。

sentences.en: No, you simpleton.
sentences.zh: 不，你这个笨蛋。

sentences.en: That's a case study of how badly that candidate did, because in a way of election where across the country Democrats are winning by something like 13 points,
sentences.zh: 那是一个关于该候选人表现有多糟糕的案例研究，因为在全国范围内民主党以大约13个百分点的优势获胜的选举中，

sentences.en: Florida should have been a place where a Democrat who was more moderate probably would have won?
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州本应是一个更温和的民主党人可能会获胜的地方？

sentences.en: That's what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, in short, Michael, I mean, think about this.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，迈克尔，想想看。

sentences.en: Florida voted for Trump by 13 points.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州以13个百分点的优势投票给了特朗普。

sentences.en: What are the other states like Florida in that range?
sentences.zh: 还有哪些州像佛罗里达州一样处于那个范围内？

sentences.en: Well, there's Texas, which voted for Trump by 14 points.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有德克萨斯州，它以14个百分点的优势投票给了特朗普。

sentences.en: Democrats won that by double digits.
sentences.zh: 民主党以两位数的优势赢得了那个州。

sentences.en: There's Ohio and Iowa and Alaska, which the Democrats have all won or are on track to win.
sentences.zh: 还有俄亥俄州、爱荷华州和阿拉斯加州，民主党都赢了或者有望获胜。

sentences.en: We can go even further down the liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们可以顺着名单继续往下看。

sentences.en: Kansas is at 16.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州是16个百分点。

sentences.en: That voted for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 那个州投票给了民主党。

sentences.en: Next on the list is South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 名单上的下一个是南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Mississippi is in this range.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州也在这个范围内。

sentences.en: When you go down the list of states from blue to red, Florida stands out as the most Democratic state in the country in the last election that the Democrats didn't win.
sentences.zh: 当你从深蓝州到深红州浏览名单时，佛罗里达州在上次选举中脱颖而出，成为民主党没有获胜的最倾向民主党的州。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so inevitably you have to ask, what is it about that candidate?
sentences.zh: 所以不可避免地你要问，那个候选人有什么问题？

sentences.en: Why didn't that Democratic candidate do what the Democratic candidates did in all these other places?
sentences.zh: 为什么那位民主党候选人没有像其他所有地方的民主党候选人那样做？

sentences.en: They were far more progressive.
sentences.zh: 他们太激进了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that the Democratic candidates who ran broadly appealing, moderate campaigns, who, you know, maybe ran as, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为那些开展了广泛吸引力、温和竞选活动的民主党候选人，你知道，也许他们以，你知道，

sentences.en: full-throated Christians with religious trainings of their own.
sentences.zh: 直言不讳的基督徒身份参选，并拥有自己的宗教背景。

sentences.en: Those are the candidates that look like they did the best in this election.
sentences.zh: 这些候选人看起来在这次选举中表现最好。

sentences.en: And some of the results are extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 而且有些结果是非凡的。

sentences.en: John Ossoff in Georgia won by nearly 20 points.
sentences.zh: 乔治亚州的乔恩·奥索夫以近20个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: And, again, I mean, imagine if I had told you a few years ago that the Democrats could win Texas,
sentences.zh: 而且，再说一次，想象一下如果几年前我告诉你民主党可以赢得德克萨斯州，

sentences.en: Kansas by more than Democrats would win in Michigan and that they wouldn't even win Florida.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州的胜幅会超过民主党在密歇根州的胜幅，而且他们甚至赢不了佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: It wouldn't make any sense if I told you that.
sentences.zh: 如果我那样告诉你，那根本说不通。

sentences.en: And the answer is the candidates.
sentences.zh: 答案就是候选人本身。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's take a quick break.
sentences.zh: 让我们快速休息一下。

sentences.en: When we come back, talk about what we have learned in this midterm about the impact of money or the lack thereof.
sentences.zh: 回来后，谈谈我们在这次中期选举中学到的关于金钱的影响，或者缺乏金钱的影响。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.zh: 我是刘温娜。

sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《连接》谜题。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》和《字母盒》游戏。

sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Nate.
sentences.zh: 内特。

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Great to see you again.
sentences.zh: 很高兴再次见到你。

sentences.en: It's been minutes.
sentences.zh: 才过了几分钟而已。

sentences.en: I want to talk about money.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈金钱。

sentences.en: We've talked a lot on the show about the financial advantage Republicans had in this midterm.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中谈了很多关于共和党在中期选举中拥有的财务优势。

sentences.en: Two to one.
sentences.zh: 二比一。

sentences.en: They had and have spent twice as much money as Democrats in all these races.
sentences.zh: 他们在所有这些竞选中花费的资金是民主党的两倍。

sentences.en: A huge cash advantage.
sentences.zh: 巨大的现金优势。

sentences.en: Did you detect any impact in the results from that financial advantage?
sentences.zh: 你有没有从结果中察觉到这种财务优势带来的任何影响？

sentences.en: It's pretty hard to find one.
sentences.zh: 很难找到影响。

sentences.en: You know, we don't have the final results yet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们还没有最终结果。

sentences.en: Maybe once we have every last bit of data and we look at it with a magnifying glass, we'll see a little bit of an effect there.
sentences.zh: 也许一旦我们掌握了所有数据并用放大镜仔细观察，我们就会看到一点点影响。

sentences.en: But it's hard to see.
sentences.zh: 但很难看出来。

sentences.en: Republicans spent, what, $500 million in Texas?
sentences.zh: 共和党在德克萨斯州花了多少钱？5亿美元？

sentences.en: And they've lost by double digits.
sentences.zh: 结果他们以两位数的差距输了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Republicans outspent Democrats in most of the crucial Senate states.
sentences.zh: 在大多数关键的参议院州，共和党的支出都超过了民主党。

sentences.en: Can I give you some examples?
sentences.zh: 我可以给你举几个例子吗？

sentences.en: Because our colleague Shane Goldmacher has this incredible spreadsheet.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的同事谢恩·戈德马赫有一份令人难以置信的电子表格。

sentences.en: Let's see it.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看。

sentences.en: He shared it with me.
sentences.zh: 他和我分享了它。

sentences.en: In Ohio, Republicans spent $100 million more than Democrats.
sentences.zh: 在俄亥俄州，共和党比民主党多花了1亿美元。

sentences.en: In Michigan, $84 million more.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州，多花了8400万美元。

sentences.en: In Texas, $200 million more than Democrats.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州，比民主党多花了2亿美元。

sentences.en: I mean, those are huge numbers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些数字太惊人了。

sentences.en: They're huge numbers.
sentences.zh: 它们是巨大的数字。

sentences.en: They're like GDP numbers.
sentences.zh: 它们就像GDP数字一样。

sentences.en: They are like GDP.
sentences.zh: 它们确实就像GDP。

sentences.en: There are small countries that couldn't afford these ad campaigns.
sentences.zh: 有些小国甚至负担不起这些广告宣传活动。

sentences.en: And again, it's hard to see the effect.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，很难看出效果。

sentences.en: And one way to look at that is to consider the races where maybe there was less spending.
sentences.zh: 观察这一点的一种方法是考虑那些支出可能较少的竞选。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: you can find some examples of a state like maybe Mississippi or Louisiana are an example of a state where the Democrats outperformed by more than a state that was more hotly contested,
sentences.zh: 你可以找到一些例子，比如密西西比州或路易斯安那州，这些州的民主党表现出的超常发挥比那些竞争更激烈的州还要多，

sentences.en: like Texas.
sentences.zh: 比如德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: But even there, the Democrats seem to outrun their prior benchmarks as much in Texas despite all the money as they do just on the other side of the state line where no money is.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那里，尽管投入了所有资金，民主党在德克萨斯州的表现似乎也和在州界另一边没有资金投入的地方一样，超过了他们之前的基准。

sentences.en: How is that possible that this money has no influence?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能？这些钱竟然没有影响力？

sentences.en: We've been trained to believe and understand that money in politics is extremely influential.
sentences.zh: 我们一直被灌输并理解政治中的金钱具有极大的影响力。

sentences.en: Well, first, I think it's worth saying that money in politics is still really influential in important ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我认为值得说的是，政治中的金钱在重要方面仍然非常有影响力。

sentences.en: And I think that even if money doesn't affect electoral outcomes in a given election,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，即使金钱在某次选举中不影响选举结果，

sentences.en: that doesn't mean it doesn't affect what our politicians support and what policies they vote for.
sentences.zh: 那并不意味着它不影响我们的政客支持什么，也不影响他们投票支持什么政策。

sentences.en: It's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, I do think it's possible for money to have relatively limited effect, especially in a midterm election,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我确实认为金钱的影响力可能相对有限，特别是在中期选举中，

sentences.en: which is dominated by highly engaged voters who often have well-informed views about the candidates and the issues and most of all have clear feelings about the president and what's happening in Washington.
sentences.zh: 中期选举由高度参与的选民所主导，他们通常对候选人和议题有充分了解的观点，最重要的是，对总统和华盛顿正在发生的事情有明确的感受。

sentences.en: And midterm elections tend to be referendums on the party in power.
sentences.zh: 而且中期选举往往是对执政党的公投。

sentences.en: If there is any takeaway from this election, it's that the public wanted to send a message to the president and do what they could to impose a check on him.
sentences.zh: 如果说这次选举有什么启示的话，那就是公众想要向总统传达一个信息，并尽其所能对他进行制衡。

sentences.en: And while the advertisements may have succeeded in raising legitimate or illegitimate, for all I know, concerns about the Democratic candidates in these races,
sentences.zh: 虽然广告可能成功地引发了对这些竞选中民主党候选人的担忧——无论这些担忧是合法的还是非法的，我不得而知，

sentences.en: it didn't change that these voters couldn't vote for a Republican in this election.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有改变这些选民在这次选举中无法投票给共和党人的事实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You could attack James Tallarico all you wanted over something he said in the state legislature in a committee meeting however many years ago.
sentences.zh: 你可以随心所欲地攻击詹姆斯·塔拉里科，就因为他多年前在州议会委员会会议上说过的话。

sentences.en: It, you're saying, wouldn't have mattered in the Texas race because people were so mad at Trump.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，在德克萨斯州的竞选中，这无关紧要，因为人们对特朗普太愤怒了。

sentences.en: When you see the same thing happening everywhere in the country, that tells you not only that the money doesn't matter,
sentences.zh: 当你看到全国各地都在发生同样的事情时，这不仅说明金钱并不重要，

sentences.en: but like that oftentimes the candidates in the campaigns don't matter unless there's something really extreme.
sentences.zh: 而且还说明，除非出现非常极端的情况，否则竞选中的候选人往往并不重要。

sentences.en: Like when you have candidates who are Democratic socialists or something,
sentences.zh: 比如当你有民主社会主义者之类的候选人时，

sentences.en: that appears to be the kind of thing that crossed the line for a critical sliver of Republican leaning voters.
sentences.zh: 这似乎就是让一小部分倾向共和党的关键选民越过底线的事情。

sentences.en: But if you didn't cross that line,
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有越过那条底线，

sentences.en: it seems that voters just weren't willing to vote for Republican or a critical chunk of voters weren't willing to vote for Republican in this election.
sentences.zh: 选民似乎就不愿投票给共和党，或者说关键的选民群体在这次选举中不愿投票给共和党。

sentences.en: I do wonder if the billionaires prone to spend this kind of money in elections will see this midterm as a turning point because it doesn't seem like a stretch to say that Elon Musk essentially flushed that money down the toilet.
sentences.zh: 我确实在想，那些倾向于在选举中投入这种资金的亿万富翁是否会将这次中期选举视为一个转折点，因为说埃隆·马斯克基本上把钱打了水漂，这似乎并不夸张。

sentences.en: So I don't think he saw a great return on that investment.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他并没有从那项投资中获得巨大的回报。

sentences.en: And it's worth also remembering that it is now the Democrats who control government in much of the country.
sentences.zh: 而且值得记住的是，现在是民主党控制着全国大部分地区的政府。

sentences.en: The Democrats have an overwhelming majority in the Congress.
sentences.zh: 民主党在国会中拥有压倒性的多数席位。

sentences.en: And I think anyone would have to say today that the Democrats are at least reasonable favorites to win the 2028 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 我认为今天任何人都不得不说，民主党至少是赢得2028年总统大选的合理热门人选。

sentences.en: And a significant reason, not the only reason, but a significant reason why Republicans have benefited so much from big money in this election is to curry favor with the president.
sentences.zh: 共和党在这次选举中从大笔资金中获益良多，一个重要的原因——虽然不是唯一原因——是为了讨好总统。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that that calculation is as clear when the president is going to leave office in two years and when they might be staring down a Democrat in the White House.
sentences.zh: 我不确定当总统两年后就要离任，而且他们可能要面对白宫里的民主党人时，这种算计是否还那么清晰。

sentences.en: Makes some sense.
sentences.zh: 有一定道理。

sentences.en: Okay, I want to end our conversation or start to end our conversation by tying up a few loose ends and pursue a few of my own lingering curiosities from this election.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想通过解决一些悬而未决的问题，并追溯一下我对这次选举中一些挥之不去的疑问，来结束或开始结束我们的谈话。

sentences.en: So if that's okay with you.
sentences.zh: 如果你不介意的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's start with Alaska and the impact of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, the one who was encouraged to run by Democrats and who is not the Dan Sullivan,
sentences.zh: 让我们从阿拉斯加州开始，谈谈选票上第二个丹·沙利文的影响，那个被民主党人鼓励参选的、不是那个丹·沙利文的人，

sentences.en: who is the incumbent Republican candidate in that Senate race.
sentences.zh: 也就是那场参议院竞选中现任的共和党候选人。

sentences.en: The last time I looked at that race, it was so close that the vote count of the second Dan Sullivan was potentially decisive.
sentences.zh: 我上次看那场竞选时，差距非常小，以至于第二个丹·沙利文的得票数可能具有决定性作用。

sentences.en: And that made me wonder if that strategy did ultimately matter.
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑那个策略最终是否真的起了作用。

sentences.en: It's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: There's a lot of vote to count left in Alaska.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加还有很多选票有待统计。

sentences.en: And in particular, it's early in mail vote, often from the far flung outlying regions of the state.
sentences.zh: 特别是，邮寄选票还处于早期阶段，通常来自该州偏远的边远地区。

sentences.en: And we expect that vote to be pretty good for the Democrat Mary Peltola.
sentences.zh: 我们预计这些选票对民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉来说相当不错。

sentences.en: And while, again, it'll take a long time before they've counted that vote,
sentences.zh: 虽然再次强调，统计这些选票还需要很长时间，

sentences.en: I would expect Peltola's lead to keep growing and potentially even grow large enough that it would be bigger than the vote cast for the other Dan Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 但我预计佩尔托拉的领先优势会持续扩大，甚至可能大到超过投给另一个丹·沙利文的票数。

sentences.en: At this point, I think it's unlikely to represent the difference in the outcome.
sentences.zh: 目前，我认为这不太可能改变最终结果。

sentences.en: And speaking of loose ends, one loose end that I've had my eye on is the fate of the independent candidates who ran for Senate in Nebraska, South Dakota, Idaho and Montana.
sentences.zh: 说到悬而未决的问题，我一直关注的一个问题是内布拉斯加州、南达科他州、爱达荷州和蒙大拿州参议院独立候选人的命运。

sentences.en: This was also part of a deliberate Democratic strategy.
sentences.zh: 这也是民主党蓄意策略的一部分。

sentences.en: In many of these states, the Democrats withdrew from the ballot.
sentences.zh: 在这些州中的许多州，民主党人退出了竞选。

sentences.en: Three of the four states, the Democrats withdrew from the ballot to set up a one-on-one contest between a Republican and an independent.
sentences.zh: 在四个州中的三个，民主党人退出了竞选，以促成共和党人和独立候选人之间的一对一竞争。

sentences.en: Because they figured the Democratic brand wasn't strong enough in those places.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为民主党的品牌在这些地方不够强大。

sentences.en: In those very Republican states.
sentences.zh: 在那些非常共和党的州。

sentences.en: And in the end, the independent candidate didn't do that well.
sentences.zh: 最终，独立候选人的表现并不好。

sentences.en: In fact, I would say that compared to like the pre-election polls and expectations,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想说的是，与选前民调和预期相比，

sentences.en: there's a case that those were some of the most disappointing results of the night for not exactly the Democrats, but at least for the Democratic voters of those states.
sentences.zh: 可以说，对于这些州的民主党选民来说，这甚至是当晚最令人失望的结果之一，虽然不完全是针对民主党本身。

sentences.en: Should the Democrats have just run Democratic candidates?
sentences.zh: 民主党人本应该直接派出民主党候选人吗？

sentences.en: Quite possibly.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: Though I don't know that we can assume the Democrats would have done better if they had done that.
sentences.zh: 虽然我不知道我们能否假设如果他们那样做，民主党会表现得更好。

sentences.en: These are very Republican states, after all,
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这些都是非常共和党的州，

sentences.en: and they're also pretty white states where maybe there aren't enough of those young and non-white voters who drove Democratic gains elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 而且它们也是相当白人的州，可能没有足够的年轻和非白人选民来推动民主党在其他地方的增长。

sentences.en: But it's hard to see a clear sign that this was some miraculous strategy that offers the way forward for the party in Red America, too.
sentences.zh: 但很难看出这是一种神奇的策略，能为该党在红色美国也提供前进的道路。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Finally, I want to ask you about polling itself.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想问你关于民调本身的问题。

sentences.en: Our polling.
sentences.zh: 我们的民调。

sentences.en: I guess your polling.
sentences.zh: 我想是你的民调。

sentences.en: We always remind listeners that polling is a snapshot in time, not a forecast, but we know it's a quite imperfect science, even in that context.
sentences.zh: 我们总是提醒听众，民调只是某一时刻的快照，而不是预测，但我们知道即使在这种背景下，它也是一门相当不完美的科学。

sentences.en: And it has failed in the past decade a few times, most notably in 2016.
sentences.zh: 而且它在过去十年中失败了几次，最著名的是2016年。

sentences.en: And there were times in this midterm election cycle, I'm not going to lie, when our polling that showed Democrats opening up leads, sometimes meaningful leads in these red states,
sentences.zh: 在这个中期选举周期中，有几次，我不撒谎，当我们的民调显示民主党人开始领先，有时在这些红色州有意义的领先时，

sentences.en: felt kind of hard to fathom.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点难以理解。

sentences.en: It felt like perhaps we were going out on a limb.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们可能是在冒险。

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And, of course, here we are, a couple days removed from a blue wave, maybe even a tsunami.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现在距离蓝色浪潮，甚至可能是海啸，已经过去几天了。

sentences.en: So let's talk about how accurate our polls in the end were or weren't.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们谈谈我们的民调最终到底准不准。

sentences.en: How do you grade yourself, my friend?
sentences.zh: 朋友，你给自己打几分？

sentences.en: Well, I don't like giving myself any pats on the back, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不喜欢自夸，迈克尔。

sentences.en: But I do think that the final polls that we released were basically spot on.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们发布的最终民调基本上是准确的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I came on the show on Tuesday or one day.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我在周二还是哪天上了节目。

sentences.en: I don't remember when it was.
sentences.zh: 我不记得是什么时候了。

sentences.en: We said it looked like a tsunami.
sentences.zh: 我们说看起来像是一场海啸。

sentences.en: And that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 结果确实如此。

sentences.en: Our final poll said that the Democrats were tighter ahead in all seven of the key Senate battlegrounds and leading by an average of five points.
sentences.zh: 我们的最终民调显示，民主党人在所有七个关键的参议院战场州都处于领先地位，平均领先五个百分点。

sentences.en: And today, the Democrats are tighter ahead in all seven states with an average lead of five points.
sentences.zh: 而今天，民主党人在所有七个州都处于领先地位，平均领先五个百分点。

sentences.en: So that's about as good as we can do.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经是我们能做到的最好程度了。

sentences.en: Mazel.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: Now, I do think there's one interesting thing that maybe helps tell the story of the election, though, in this,
sentences.zh: 现在，我确实认为有一件有趣的事情可能有助于讲述这次选举的故事，

sentences.en: which is that although our final polls were as good as we can ever hope for and we really can't do better, polls will never be perfect.
sentences.zh: 那就是，尽管我们的最终民调是我们所能期望的最好的，我们真的无法做得更好，但民调永远不会完美。

sentences.en: It's just not possible.
sentences.zh: 这根本不可能。

sentences.en: The polls we took like three weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我们大约三周前做的民调。

sentences.en: I remember this.
sentences.zh: 我记得这个。

sentences.en: They weren't quite so perfect.
sentences.zh: 它们并没有那么完美。

sentences.en: They weren't bad.
sentences.zh: 它们并不坏。

sentences.en: They're better than a lot of the other polls still.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然比许多其他民调要好。

sentences.en: But they did underestimate the Democrats a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实稍微低估了民主党人。

sentences.en: And if you go back to September, even bigger underestimate.
sentences.zh: 如果你回到九月，低估得更严重。

sentences.en: Were they underestimating the Democratic votes or were the Democratic votes themselves not ready to declare themselves to pollsters?
sentences.zh: 他们是低估了民主党的选票，还是民主党选民自己还没准备好向民调机构表明立场？

sentences.en: I think the latter is probably the better explanation.
sentences.zh: 我认为后者可能是更好的解释。

sentences.en: And thank you for bringing up that possibility.
sentences.zh: 感谢你提出这种可能性。

sentences.en: We didn't change our polling over this period, but we saw that the results kept getting better for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我们在这段时间内没有改变我们的民调方式，但我们看到结果对民主党人来说越来越好。

sentences.en: I think we called it a surge in our final polls.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在最终民调中称之为激增。

sentences.en: And I think the likeliest explanation is that this big group of voters, traditionally Republican voters who were dissatisfied with the president or alternately in some states,
sentences.zh: 我认为最可能的解释是，这大批选民，即那些对总统不满的传统共和党选民，或者在某些州，

sentences.en: the traditionally Democratic voters who were dissatisfied with their Democratic nominees in a place like Maine or Michigan.
sentences.zh: 那些对缅因州或密歇根州等地的民主党提名人不满的传统民主党选民，

sentences.en: But as they got down to decision time, they all sort of resolved on the same answer, which is I have to vote Democratic to be a check on the president.
sentences.zh: 但当他们到了做决定的时候，他们都得出了同样的结论，那就是我必须投票给民主党，以制衡总统。

sentences.en: This helps me understand why we poll as frequently as we do, given how expensive and cumbersome polling is.
sentences.zh: 这让我明白了为什么我们进行如此频繁的民调，考虑到民调是多么昂贵和繁琐。

sentences.en: We keep polling.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在进行民调。

sentences.en: And how we still don't know if it's right even when we do it.
sentences.zh: 而且即使我们做了，我们仍然不知道它是否正确。

sentences.en: But we keep polling because people keep making up their minds.
sentences.zh: 但我们一直在进行民调，因为人们一直在改变主意。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, these election results are extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，再次强调，这些选举结果是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: And they are results that you would never have predicted.
sentences.zh: 而且这些结果是你永远无法预测的。

sentences.en: I at least would have never have predicted that Texas could be easily for Democrats and so on without the polls to say it.
sentences.zh: 至少如果没有民调数据，我永远无法预测德克萨斯州会轻易倒向民主党等等。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, Nate.
sentences.zh: 好吧，内特。

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: On those polls.
sentences.zh: 关于那些民调。

sentences.en: Because in some future conversation about some future election, it won't be this good again.
sentences.zh: 因为在未来关于未来某次选举的谈话中，它不会再这么好了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They will be wrong again.
sentences.zh: 它们会再次出错。

sentences.en: I've been on that side before.
sentences.zh: 我以前也经历过那一面。

sentences.en: The losses will happen.
sentences.zh: 失败总会发生。

sentences.en: And so we have to take our wins when they come.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须在胜利到来时享受它们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: We really take them when the losses come, don't we?
